key_highlights: ASX finished flat with miners rising and oil stocks struggling; IDP plunged on the session (#32)
Tech stocks led ASX higher following Wall Street surge; oil snapped its losing run (#59)
RBA rate hikes continue to squeeze household spending, pressuring consumer discretionary and REITs (#54)
Saudi oil shock sends Australian fuel prices surging, raising inflation and cost-of-living concerns (#62, #26)
BoomRay signs $900m Novartis radioligand therapy deal, a landmark for ASX-listed medtech (#1)
Gold and rare earths miners active: Critical Resources surges on Suriname grab, Aurum raises $52.5m, Platina banks Rio cheque (#40, #41, #61)
Australian flash PMI sags, signalling softening domestic demand (#50)
Qatar LNG loss revives Timor-Leste and Argentina gas projects, positive for ASX energy names (#70)
Fixed mortgage rates finding more room to fall; CD rates up to 4.40% APY (#6, #4)
Federal and state governments face mounting debt pressures (#65)

sectors.trend: Miners rose on the session; gold miners (Critical Resources, Aurum, Platina) and rare earths (Critica/Jupiter) saw strong momentum. Oil-linked miners under pressure from falling crude.
sectors.implications: Gold and critical-minerals names offer relative strength amid geopolitical uncertainty. BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX supported by iron ore but watch oil-linked exposure. Critica (CR8.AX) and Jupiter (JUP.AX) offtake progress is a positive catalyst.

sectors.trend: RBA rate hikes squeezing household spending; fixed mortgage rates finding room to fall; CD rates at 4.40% APY. Net interest margin pressure on banks.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin compression as deposit competition intensifies. Falling fixed rates may support refinance volumes but compress NIMs. Watch RBA next meeting.

sectors.trend: Oil stocks struggled on ASX; Saudi oil shock spiking Australian fuel prices; Qatar LNG loss revives Timor-Leste projects. Commonwealth to fund abandoned WA oil platform.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX, XAR.AX face headwinds from falling crude. Timor-Leste LNG revival is a medium-term positive for gas infrastructure names. Fuel price surge risks re-igniting inflation.

sectors.trend: BoomRay–Novartis $900m radioligand deal is a sector-defining event; Syngenis gains precision medicine firepower.
sectors.implications: BMY.AX (BoomRay) validates ASX medtech pipeline. CSL.AX and other healthcare names benefit from global radioligand therapy momentum. Syngenis (SYG.AX) gains strategic optionality.

sectors.trend: Tech stocks led ASX higher post Wall Street surge. $16b Aussie tech firm faces China-link controversy. AI infrastructure (Vicor +18%) and Big Tech cash flows ($2T) in focus.
sectors.implications: ASX tech names benefit from global AI capex cycle but China-link risks create idiosyncratic volatility. Monitor 29 (Aussie tech firm) for regulatory overhang.

sectors.trend: Jetstar industrial action (waiving baggage/seat fees); Qantas to launch Sydney–NY non-stop. RBA hikes squeezing discretionary spend.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX benefits from new trans-Pacific route but faces Jetstar (JLH.AX) competitive pressure. Consumer staples (WES.AX, WOW.AX) may see defensive rotation.

sectors.trend: Rising listings and falling demand driving property prices lower. RBA rate environment still restrictive.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX, SPG.AX) face occupancy and valuation headwinds. Falling prices may create entry points for long-term buyers but near-term sentiment is weak.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain gold allocation as geopolitical hedge
defensive_moves.rationale: Trump-Xi meeting, US-China tensions, and global economic wariness of America support safe-haven demand

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to range-trade with sector rotation: tech and gold/rare earths outperforming, oil and consumer lagging. Fuel price shock and PMI softness cap upside. RBA policy path is the key swing factor. IDP's plunge signals idiosyncratic risk in small-caps.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautiously constructive for commodity-linked and healthcare names. Timor-Leste LNG revival and AI capex cycle provide structural tailwinds. However, government debt pressures, household balance sheet stress from RBA hikes, and global geopolitical fragmentation cap broad market gains. Property sector remains a laggard.
